build.environment: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS under WSL, TeX Live 2023, pdfTeX 1.40.25, latexmk 4.83, Poppler 24.02.0
build.result: Two clean builds from the extracted source ZIP produced byte-identical PDFs with no final LaTeX or layout warnings. Inspected PNG renders of every page and checked that the title and abstract agree with the metadata.

endpoint_minima.result: Five million four hundred seventy-five thousand two hundred eight minima through dimension 200, including 2,145 ordinary-forcing signatures. All 1,188 dimension-30 minima and a brute endpoint test on 401 signatures through dimension 20 agree.

full_historical_counts.result: An integral-breakpoint enumeration reproduced all 1,188 historical rows, including 8,073,364 candidate polygons, 3,846,011 surviving polygons, and the minimum p-ranks.

moment_covers.result: The former replays three rational residues, the split p=19 case, and 69 bounded branch multisets across 20 combinations. The latter checks the split nonordinary p=73 selection and connected-conductor examples at 37 in orders 342, 12,663 and 468,540.

pfaffian_curve.result: Recomputed the genus-four cyclic covering character counts and relative Frobenius quartics at 7 and 13, checked ordinary middle coefficients and the S4 factorization witnesses, distinguished the two absolute Frobenius fields by splitting at 2, and verified the ordinary reduction at the inert prime 11. The article supplies the specialization argument from these certificates to the geometric endomorphism ring.

replay_scope: All five commands were executed from the archived supplement in Python 3.12.3 or PARI/GP 2.15.4. The programs check the stated finite examples. The adjoint norm and p-rank results, CM norm and numerical bounds, twelvefold construction, fourfold density theorem and finite-field Pfaffian sharpness use written arguments.

pdf_only_internal_review.context: The complete text extracted from the compiled PDF, selected rendered pages and the five neutral reader prompts. The final reader received rendered pages 1, 5–8, 10 and 14. No repository material or previous conversation was supplied, and the readers made no tool calls.
findings: Recovered the factorwise weighted adjoint bound, the exact half-slope and p-rank formulas, the original-field splitting criterion and the separate fourfold and numerical CM conclusions.
Explained the effect of a flat active factor on the tensor weights, the unpowered block trace product in the original-field case, and the finite-integer norm exclusions.

Located the one-step crystalline comparison as the hardest step. The candidate reader asked why the comparison over an unramified tensor-defining extension still applies to the one-step Frobenius. The revision identifies the geometric special point, the Frobenius-invariant tensors and the one-step class explicitly, and locates admissibility in Kisin–Madapusi Pera–Shin. The final reader recovered this argument and identified its cited inputs for specialist review.

Distinguished eventual ordinarity, the original-field tensor criterion with its extra hypotheses, the full-endomorphism hypothesis for the fourfold, and the finite-field scope of the sharp higher-rank Pfaffian bound. Identified the split cubic real-multiplication case as a remaining density question.

The first reader requested an explicit compositum in the unbalanced fourfold discussion. The revision writes K tau(E). The final reader flagged missing absolute-value bars in the extracted rank-two trace formula. The rendered page 18 and the LaTeX source both contain the bars, which were lost by text extraction. The finite replays and their proof scopes were checked separately from the PDF-only review.
pdf_only_internal_review.revisions_and_rechecks: Expanded the one-step Frobenius argument and stated the unbalanced compositum explicitly. The cited Kisin–Madapusi Pera–Shin statements were inspected in the linked Harvard author copy, where Proposition 1.3.6 applies to each geometric special point, Section 1.3.7 constructs the one-step class and Lemma 1.3.8 gives admissibility. A fresh final reader followed the revised route and found no internal contradiction in the displayed headline arguments.

remaining: Specialist review of the tensor comparison, adjoint and Pfaffian arguments, the corestriction realization over a number field, the numerical minima, and priority.
Density of one flat active factor at completely split primes with three independent active labels in the cubic real multiplication case.

additional_arithmetic_check.result: Both symbolic equalities hold over Z[p], checking the determinant factors 1/p and 1 in the finite-field sharpness construction by resultants. The manuscript gives the algebraic derivation.
